primary_number: ~12.0M for Greater Jakarta (Jabodetabek) in 2024; ~14.3M at 2019 national-MC peak
publisher: World Bank (2019) — Aspiring Indonesia: Expanding the Middle Class, using 2016 Susenas microdata
methodology_note: World Bank 2019 report (Figure E.9, Figure 3.3) states ~13 million MC in Greater Jakarta (Jabodetabek) in 2016, equal to 25% of the national MC total (52-53.6M). The report also states 76% of national MC is urban, and two-thirds of urban MC lives in major metropolitan agglomerations. BPS confirmed the national MC peaked at 57.33M in 2019 then declined to 47.85M by 2024 (Mar 2024 Susenas). Scaling the Greater Jakarta 25% share to the 2024 national total gives ~11.6-12.0M for Greater Jakarta in 2024. The claimed 13.5-14.5M range corresponds closely to Greater Jakarta at the 2019 national MC peak (57.33M × 25% = 14.3M) — suggesting the original forward-scaling by Claude inadvertently anchored on a ~2019 peak rather than the 2024 post-decline figure. No provincial or city-level disaggregation of the 47.85M figure was released by BPS in October 2024 (BPS press release confirmed 403 Forbidden; national total only). No SMERU or BCG/McKinsey post-2019 city-level breakdown found within search budget.

city_breakdown.surabaya: Identified in World Bank report as a city with MC rate 'significantly higher' than AMC rate, but no absolute headcount given in the extractable text — chart data not recoverable from PDF extraction
city_breakdown.other_tier_1_total: Two-thirds of urban MC (40.6M in 2016) live in major metro agglomerations = ~27M total metro MC in 2016; minus Greater Jakarta (13M) = ~14M for all other major metros combined in 2016; scaled to 2024 → ~12.5M for all non-Jakarta major metros
